editionLabel: Days of Wonder English rules, 2015 file
location: Setting up the game, final starting-player and purple-temple instructions
firstPlayerRule: Start with whoever saw a relic most recently, then take turns clockwise.
officialTieBreak: If nobody in the group has ever seen a relic, the rules instead use the most recent visit to a shrine or temple.
clarifications: Choose the starting player before turning over the top tile of each purple temple.
uncertainty: The official alternative covers nobody having seen a relic. The passage does not resolve equally recent visits or nobody meeting the alternative criterion.
evidenceNotes: The English page identifies both the relic criterion and the shrine/temple alternative. Copyright and layout text identify the 2015 file; the hosting path is not an edition date. The starting passage and nearby setup context were visually inspected.

editionLabel: Days of Wonder English rules, 2015 V2 file
location: Setting up the game; Starting the game; III. Sending Ships Out
firstPlayerRule: Whoever last visited a port in real life starts and takes the first-player marker. Turns proceed clockwise.
clarifications: The first player moves the game-turn marker forward at the start of each round.
On everyone's first turn, skip phases 1 and 2 and begin with phase 3, Sending Ships Out.
evidenceNotes: All three cited pages were viewed. The port visit selects the starter; the first-turn phase exception applies to every player. The file's layout identifies English V2, 2015.

gameName: Cleopatra and the Society of Architects
editionLabel: Original Days of Wonder English edition, copyright 2006
firstPlayerRule: The rules give the first turn to the player with the best Egyptian credentials; otherwise, start with the youngest player. Play continues clockwise.
officialTieBreak: The youngest player is the rulebook's stated alternative.
clarifications: The credentials are playful examples, such as a pet mummified crocodile or a hieroglyphic library. The rulebook supplies no scoring system for them.
This answer covers the original Days of Wonder edition, not the later Deluxe Edition.
uncertainty: The passage does not explain a tie between equally young players.
evidenceNotes: PDF page 4 is printed page 3. The examples were read in context and are not interpreted as a nationality or ancestry test. The source credits carry copyright 2006.

editionLabel: Days of Wonder English rules, 2015 file
location: Setup, whistle and first-player paragraph; three- and four-player notes
firstPlayerRule: The most recent person to board a real train starts and takes the miniature whistle. Play goes clockwise.
clarifications: After each round of players' turns, the person who acted last takes the whistle and starts the next round.
evidenceNotes: The rendered page has printed number 2, even though its layout-production stamp says Page 3. The rulebook uses 'turn' for the full round here; the summary distinguishes that round from one player's action. The three- and four-player adjustments on the same page do not replace the starting criterion.

editionLabel: Days of Wonder refreshed English rules, 7281N publisher download
firstPlayerRule: The group chooses its own method for deciding who starts. Continue clockwise from that player.
clarifications: This refreshed rulebook leaves the choice of starting method to the group. Choosing randomly is one way to use that permission.
Check your edition: the separate 15th Anniversary rulebook instead starts with whoever has visited the most European countries.

location: Starting the game on the left of the spread; I. The first turn on the right
firstPlayerRule: Whoever has the pointiest ears takes the first turn. Continue clockwise around the table.
clarifications: The same first player advances the game-turn marker when a new round begins.
evidenceNotes: The PDF uses spreads: PDF page 2 contains printed pages 2 and 3. The starting-player paragraph is on printed page 2. Copyright on the final source page ends in 2018.
